source_name: OSHP / PRB – Procurement Review Body, complaint & decision search
why_relevant: The appeal file is often richer than the notice: OSHP records contracting authority, procurement subject, estimated value, appellant (losing bidder), review-panel composition, expert reviewers, cited PPL articles and outcome. Searchable/filterable by contracting authority, tender category and value — the single best structured view of who lost which banking/IT tender and why.

source_name: OSHP – Reports / statistics module (complaints by year, by decision, blacklist)
why_relevant: Aggregate complaint volumes and outcome distributions (e.g. 1,292 complaints in 2024 vs 1,089 in 2023) give a denominator for market-contestation analysis, and the blacklist report identifies economic operators barred from bidding — directly relevant to vendor due diligence in banking IT.

source_name: Demokraci Plus (D+) – OSHP decisions database (oshp.dplus.org)
why_relevant: Civil-society re-publication of OSHP rulings with far better filtering than the official site: filter by publication date, contract value range, contracting authority, appellant, individual panel members, experts and cited legal articles. Excellent for finding banking/payments appeals and for detecting panel-level patterns. Caveat: last update observed as Jan 2024, so it is a historical corpus, not live.

source_name: Demokraci Plus (D+) – procurement integrity research reports
why_relevant: D+ publishes analytical reports on procurement integrity and irregularities (e.g. 'Integriteti në Prokurim Publik: Sfidat dhe Parregullsitë', Aug 2025) that name authorities, patterns of single-bid awards and OSHP behaviour — context that no raw notice conveys.

source_name: BQK annual financial statements + external audit opinion
why_relevant: BQK's audited financial statements expose capitalised IT/payment-infrastructure assets, intangible software, operating expenditure lines and commitments — an indirect but reliable read on the size and timing of payment-system investment, usable when the tender itself is not published.

source_name: Gazeta Zyrtare e Republikës së Kosovës (Official Gazette) – procurement & central bank laws
why_relevant: Authoritative consolidated text of Law 04/L-042 on Public Procurement, Law 03/L-209 on the Central Bank, Law 05/L-055 on the Auditor General/NAO, and Law 02/L-44 on concessions — the statutory basis defining who must publish what, appeal deadlines, and BQK's procurement autonomy. Multilingual (sq/sr/en).

source_name: Prokurimi i Hapur (Open Procurement Kosovo) – Lëvizja FOL / Kutia
why_relevant: Structured, queryable re-publication of Kosovo public contracts by buyer, supplier and municipality, collected automatically since 2018 via an API. Lets you go supplier-first ('which vendors sell to which public buyers') rather than notice-first. Caveat: last update observed 27 Apr 2023 — verify freshness before operational use.

source_name: KALLXO.com (BIRN Kosova) – procurement & KRPP/OSHP investigative tag pages
why_relevant: Investigative journalism that names contracts, disqualified bidders, annulled tenders and OSHP re-evaluations, often before or instead of official publication. Tag pages act as a low-cost monitoring feed for procurement scandals touching regulators and financial-sector suppliers.

source_name: KOHA.net – Zyra Kombëtare e Auditimit tag feed
why_relevant: Fast pointer to newly published NAO audit reports and their procurement findings; useful as a change-detection trigger for the zka-rks.org crawl rather than as a data source in itself.

source_name: SIGMA/OECD assessments of Kosovo public procurement & external audit
why_relevant: SIGMA (OECD/EU) peer assessments describe the institutional reality of Kosovo's procurement and audit system — data quality, publication compliance, OSHP independence — which calibrates how much to trust the primary sources and where systematic gaps in the record exist.

source_name: US ITA Country Commercial Guide – Kosovo: Selling to the Public Sector
why_relevant: Concise English-language orientation to Kosovo's procurement institutions, thresholds and appeal route (KRPP, AQP, OSHP), useful for validating the actor map and for onboarding non-Albanian-speaking analysts. Not a data source.

source_name: BQK – Interbank Payment System operating scheme page (ATS/RTGS/ACH)
why_relevant: Defines the technical objects BQK actually buys and upgrades — ATS since 1 July 2016, comprising RTGS and ACH components. Provides the exact terminology (sistemi ndërbankar i pagesave, ATS, SPN) needed to match future tender titles and audit findings to payment infrastructure.

source_name: Kuvendi i Kosovës – Drejtoria për Prokurim / Committee on Public Finance Oversight
why_relevant: The Assembly is both a contracting authority (its own procurement directorate publishes notices) and the body that receives NAO and KRPP reports through the Committee on Public Finance Oversight; committee transcripts and hearing materials often contain procurement detail not in the reports themselves.

source_name: Contracting-authority self-publication of OSHP decisions (e.g. Ministry of Health document store)
why_relevant: Demonstrates a recoverable pattern: individual contracting authorities re-host OSHP decision PDFs (case-numbered, e.g. 'OSHP: 2023/0898') in their own document stores. When the OSHP site is incomplete or a decision is withdrawn, these mirrors preserve the appeal record.

source_name: Telegrafi — Ekonomi / tag feeds (Banka Qendrore e Kosovës, Shoqata e Bankave të Kosovës)
why_relevant: Highest-traffic Albanian-language Kosovo news portal; publishes bank press releases, signing ceremonies (nënshkruhet marrëveshja/kontrata), digitalisation announcements and CBK/BQK news near-verbatim and fast. Entity tag pages act as ready-made per-actor feeds (e.g. /tag/banka-qendrore-e-kosoves/, /tag/shoqata-e-bankave-te-kosoves/), which makes it a low-cost weak-signal tripwire for private-bank IT and payments contracts that never reach a public register.

source_name: Ekonomia Online (ekonomiaonline.com)
why_relevant: Dedicated Albanian-language economic news agency based in Prishtina, covering daily economic events, banking sector results, investments and business technology. Being economy-specialised, it carries bank/vendor announcements that generalist portals skip, and is a likely first public trace of a payments or core-banking deal.

source_name: KALLXO.com (BIRN Kosova / Internews) — procurement investigations
why_relevant: The single most procurement-literate Albanian-language outlet in Kosovo. Runs sustained investigative reporting on tender awards, contract cancellations after award, negotiated procedures without competition, and OSHP/KRPP decisions — naming contracting authority, winning company and contract value. Also maintains topical tag pages (e.g. KRPP) usable as feeds. Directly on-topic for award notices and disputes.

source_name: Preportr (Qendra për Gazetari Hulumtuese / COHU)
why_relevant: Investigative outlet specialising in public spending, procurement contracts and conflict-of-interest in Kosovo. Long-form pieces typically reconstruct contract chains and supplier ownership, which is exactly the indirect evidence needed where the register is thin. Referenced in the seed framing; URL asserted from prior knowledge, treat as unverified until the liveness pass runs.

source_name: KosovaPress (agjencia e lajmeve) — Ekonomi
why_relevant: National Albanian-language news agency; carries bank and fintech sector items including banking innovation/AI and data coverage, and reprints institutional press releases. Agency copy propagates to other portals, so it is a good upstream capture point for first-publication timestamps.

source_name: Koha.net / Koha Ditore — Ekonomi
why_relevant: One of Kosovo's oldest and most editorially serious Albanian-language outlets, with a standing economy desk that covers CBK reporting, banking sector performance and state procurement controversies. Useful as a credibility cross-check against faster, less careful portals.

source_name: Klan Kosova — Ekonomi
why_relevant: One of the most popular private broadcasters in Kosovo, with an online economy section. Broadcast interviews with bank executives and ministers often surface procurement/modernisation plans months before any documentary trace, making it a genuine weak-signal channel.

source_name: Insajderi.org
why_relevant: Albanian-language portal with an investigative bent covering Kosovo news, business and economics. Publishes leaks and institutional-decision stories (e.g. complaint/appeal rulings) that can expose tender disputes between contracting authorities and suppliers.

source_name: IndeksOnline
why_relevant: High-velocity Albanian-language news portal in Kosovo built around speed and originality of breaking items. Low editorial filter means bank/vendor press releases and contract-signing photo-ops appear here early; value is timing, not analysis.
